body:
I took a quick attempt at this.

Maybe `Vector<T>::ordered_insert` would be a simple fix here? It keeps `tiles_ids` sorted with a bisect + insert instead of re-sorting the whole vector on every `create_tile()` call.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1a0d5d8c93ed4ccfa18e2850a465bd64a7be5295/core/templates/vector.h#L200-L203

I tested it with the script mentioned above.

```powershell
#before
Godot Engine v4.8.dev.custom_build.a46e3a103 (2026-09-14 14:14:26 UTC) - https://godotengine.org

  1000 tiles:    0.074 s
  2000 tiles:    0.357 s
  4000 tiles:    1.670 s
  8000 tiles:    7.242 s
 16000 tiles:   31.224 s
 32000 tiles:  150.158 s
#after
Godot Engine v4.8.dev.custom_build.a46e3a103 (2026-09-14 14:14:26 UTC) - https://godotengine.org

  1000 tiles:    0.009 s
  2000 tiles:    0.015 s
  4000 tiles:    0.035 s
  8000 tiles:    0.079 s
 16000 tiles:    0.215 s
 32000 tiles:    0.434 s
```

```diff

Index: modules/tilemap/tile_set.cpp
IDEA additional info:
Subsystem: com.intellij.openapi.diff.impl.patch.CharsetEP
<+>UTF-8
===================================================================
diff --git a/modules/tilemap/tile_set.cpp b/modules/tilemap/tile_set.cpp
--- a/modules/tilemap/tile_set.cpp	(revision a46e3a10330d202abce5dbb4d426d684d79e5f56)
+++ b/modules/tilemap/tile_set.cpp	(date 1789410313094)
@@ -5010,8 +5010,7 @@
 
 	// Create and resize the tile.
 	tiles.insert(p_atlas_coords, tad);
-	tiles_ids.push_back(p_atlas_coords);
-	tiles_ids.sort();
+	tiles_ids.ordered_insert(p_atlas_coords);
 
 	_create_coords_mapping_cache(p_atlas_coords);
 	_queue_update_padded_texture();

```
Hope this helps!
